questions.questionTextEn: According to the Heisenberg uncertainty principle, the minimum product of uncertainties in the $x$-component of position ($\Delta x$) and the $x$-component of linear momentum ($\Delta p_x$) is
questions.explanationEn: The Heisenberg uncertainty relation states $\Delta x \cdot \Delta p_x \ge \frac{\hbar}{2} = \frac{h}{4\pi}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: If $y = x^x$ for $x > 0$, then the value of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = 1$ is
questions.explanationEn: Taking natural logarithms: $\ln y = x\ln x$. Differentiating gives $\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx} = \ln x + 1$, so $\frac{dy}{dx} = x^x(1 + \ln x)$. At $x = 1$, $\frac{dy}{dx} = 1^1(1 + 0) = 1$.

questions.questionTextEn: The value of $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin(5x)}{3x}$ is
questions.explanationEn: Using the standard limit $\lim_{u \to 0} \frac{\sin u}{u} = 1$, we write $\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin(5x)}{3x} = \frac{5}{3}\lim_{x \to 0}\frac{\sin(5x)}{5x} = \frac{5}{3}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A box contains $5$ red balls and $3$ blue balls. Two balls are drawn sequentially without replacement. The probability that both drawn balls are red is
questions.explanationEn: The probability that the first ball is red is $\frac{5}{8}$. Given the first is red, $4$ red balls remain out of $7$, so the probability that the second is also red is $\frac{4}{7}$. Thus $P = \frac{5}{8} \times \frac{4}{7} = \frac{20}{56} = \frac{5}{14}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A fair coin is tossed $4$ independent times. The probability of obtaining **at least $3$ heads** is
questions.explanationEn: Using the binomial distribution with $n = 4$ and $p = 1/2$: $P(X \ge 3) = P(X = 3) + P(X = 4) = \binom{4}{3}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^4 + \binom{4}{4}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^4 = \frac{4 + 1}{16} = \frac{5}{16}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Using the canonical commutation relation $[\hat{x}, \hat{p}_x] = i\hbar$, the commutator $[\hat{x}^2, \hat{p}_x]$ simplifies to
questions.explanationEn: Using $[AB, C] = A[B, C] + [A, C]B$, we obtain $[\hat{x}^2, \hat{p}_x] = \hat{x}[\hat{x}, \hat{p}_x] + [\hat{x}, \hat{p}_x]\hat{x} = \hat{x}(i\hbar) + (i\hbar)\hat{x} = 2i\hbar\hat{x}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: If $y(x)$ satisfies the linear first-order differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = 3x$ ($x > 0$) with $y(1) = 2$, then $y(2)$ is equal to
questions.explanationEn: The integrating factor is $\mu(x) = e^{\int (1/x)\,dx} = x$. Multiplying through gives $\frac{d}{dx}(xy) = 3x^2 \implies xy = x^3 + C$. Using $y(1) = 2$ gives $2 = 1 + C \implies C = 1$, so $y(x) = x^2 + \frac{1}{x}$. At $x = 2$, $y(2) = 4 + 0.5 = 4.5$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The volume of the parallelepiped formed by the three vectors $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j}$, $\vec{b} = 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}$, and $\vec{c} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{k}$ is
questions.explanationEn: The volume is the magnitude of the scalar triple product $|\vec{a}\cdot(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})| = \left|\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \end{vmatrix}\right| = |2(6 - 0) - 1(0 - 1) + 0| = |12 + 1| = 13$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about hydrogen atom orbitals is/are correct?
optionsEn: The $3s$ orbital has $2$ spherical (radial) nodes and $0$ angular nodes.
The $3p_z$ orbital has $1$ radial node and $1$ nodal plane (the $xy$-plane).
The $3d_{z^2}$ orbital has $0$ radial nodes and $2$ conical nodal surfaces.
In a hydrogen atom, the energy of the $3d$ orbital is higher than that of the $3s$ orbital.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) True:** For $3s$ ($n=3, l=0$), radial nodes $= 3 - 0 - 1 = 2$, angular nodes $= 0$.
- **(B) True:** For $3p_z$ ($n=3, l=1$), radial nodes $= 1$ and angular node is the $xy$-plane ($z = 0$).
- **(C) True:** For $3d_{z^2}$ ($n=3, l=2$), radial nodes $= 0$ and the angular part $(3\cos^2\theta - 1)$ vanishes on two cones ($\theta \approx 54.7^\circ$ and $125.3^\circ$).
- **(D) False:** In a one-electron hydrogen atom, $3s, 3p,$ and $3d$ are strictly degenerate.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For two events $E_1$ and $E_2$ with $P(E_1) > 0$ and $P(E_2) > 0$, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: If $E_1$ and $E_2$ are independent, then $P(E_1 \cap E_2) = P(E_1)P(E_2)$.
If $E_1$ and $E_2$ are mutually exclusive, then $P(E_1 \cap E_2) = 0$.
If $E_1$ and $E_2$ are mutually exclusive, they must also be independent.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A), (B), (C) True:** Standard probability addition rule, independence definition, and mutual exclusivity definition.
- **(D) False:** If $E_1$ and $E_2$ are mutually exclusive with $P(E_1) > 0, P(E_2) > 0$, then $P(E_1 \cap E_2) = 0 \neq P(E_1)P(E_2)$, so they cannot be independent.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For the linear centrosymmetric molecule $\text{CO}_2$, the correct statement(s) about its fundamental vibrational modes is/are
optionsEn: The symmetric stretching mode is Raman-active and IR-inactive.
The asymmetric stretching mode is IR-active and Raman-inactive.
The bending mode is doubly degenerate and IR-active.
All $4$ vibrational modes are simultaneously IR- and Raman-active.
questions.explanationEn:
$\text{CO}_2$ ($D_{\infty h}$) has $3(3) - 5 = 4$ normal modes and obeys the rule of mutual exclusion:
- **(A) True:** Symmetric stretch changes polarizability ($\alpha$) but not dipole moment ($\mu$) $\implies$ Raman-active, IR-inactive.
- **(B) True:** Asymmetric stretch changes $\mu$ but not $\alpha$ $\implies$ IR-active, Raman-inactive.
- **(C) True:** Bending occurs in two orthogonal planes (doubly degenerate) and changes $\mu$ $\implies$ IR-active.
- **(D) False:** Contradicts the rule of mutual exclusion.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following molecule(s) is/are classified as a **spherical top** ($I_a = I_b = I_c$)?
questions.explanationEn: Spherical tops belong to cubic point groups ($T_d, O_h, I_h$) and have three equal principal moments of inertia ($I_a = I_b = I_c$). $\text{CH}_4$ ($T_d$), $\text{SF}_6$ ($O_h$), and tetrahedral $\text{P}_4$ ($T_d$) are spherical tops, whereas $\text{NH}_3$ ($C_{3v}$) is an oblate symmetric top ($I_a = I_b < I_c$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn:
The energy of a single photon of wavelength $400\text{ nm}$ is _______ $\text{eV}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
[Given: $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$, $c = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $1\text{ eV} = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}$]
questions.explanationEn: Using $E = \frac{hc}{\lambda}$, $E = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34} \times 3.0 \times 10^8}{400 \times 10^{-9} \times 1.602 \times 10^{-19}} = 3.102\text{ eV} \approx 3.10\text{ eV}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The determinant of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 \end{pmatrix}$ is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: The determinant of an upper-triangular matrix is simply the product of its main diagonal entries: $2 \times 4 \times 5 = 40$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: On a $300\text{ MHz}$ $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrometer, a proton signal resonates $2160\text{ Hz}$ downfield from TMS. Its chemical shift $\delta$ is _______ $\text{ppm}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: The chemical shift in ppm is $\delta = \frac{\Delta\nu\text{ (Hz)}}{\nu_0\text{ (MHz)}} = \frac{2160}{300} = 7.20\text{ ppm}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The degeneracy of the $J = 4$ rotational energy level of a linear diatomic molecule is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Each rotational level $J$ of a linear rotor has a $(2J + 1)$-fold spatial degeneracy corresponding to $M_J = -J, \dots, +J$. For $J = 4$, the degeneracy is $2(4) + 1 = 9$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of vibrational degrees of freedom in a methane ($\text{CH}_4$) molecule is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Methane is a non-linear polyatomic molecule with $N = 5$ atoms, so it has $3N - 6 = 3(5) - 6 = 9$ vibrational degrees of freedom.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry I: Quantum Chemistry, Spectroscopy & Math (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A discrete random variable $X$ takes the values $1, 2, 3, 4$ with probabilities $k, 2k, 3k, 4k$, respectively. The expected value $E[X]$ is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Normalization of probabilities requires $k + 2k + 3k + 4k = 10k = 1 \implies k = 0.1$. The expected value is $E[X] = \sum x P(x) = 1(0.1) + 2(0.2) + 3(0.3) + 4(0.4) = 0.1 + 0.4 + 0.9 + 1.6 = 3$.
